title: Conditioning & Stability
description: Condition number of a problem, forward and backward stability, error propagation, difference quotients.
html:
⚠️ Conditioning & Stability

1. Conditioning (Problem)

$$\kappa(x) = \left|\frac{x f'(x)}{f(x)}\right|, \qquad \frac{|\Delta y|}{|y|} \approx \kappa(x)\frac{|\Delta x|}{|x|}$$

Good: $\kappa \lesssim 1$. Bad: $\kappa \gg 1$. You lose about $\log_{10}\kappa$ decimal digits.

Examples

$\kappa_{\sqrt x} = \tfrac12$, $\kappa_{x^n} = n$, $\kappa_{e^x} = |x|$, $\kappa_{\ln x} = 1/|\ln x|$, $\kappa_{x-1} = |x/(x-1)|$.

2. Error Propagation

$$|\Delta f| \lesssim \sum_i \left|\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}\right|\Delta x_i$$

Multiplication/division: relative errors add up. Subtraction of nearly equal numbers: ill-conditioned.

3. Stability (Algorithm)

Forward and Backward Error

Backward stable: result = exact result for data perturbed by $O(u)$. Then: forward error $\lesssim \kappa \cdot u$.

Example: $I_n = 1 - nI_{n-1}$ forward: error $\times n!$ (unstable). Backward $I_{n-1} = (1 - I_n)/n$: error $\div n$ (stable).

4. Numerical Differentiation

$$D_+ = \frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} = f' + \tfrac h2 f'', \qquad D_0 = \frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h} = f' + \tfrac{h^2}{6} f'''$$

Total error = truncation error $\sim h^p$ + rounding error $\sim u/h$. Optimum: $h \approx \sqrt{\varepsilon_{\text{mach}}} \approx 10^{-8}$ (forward), $h \approx \varepsilon^{1/3} \approx 10^{-5}$ (central).

5. Typical Mistakes

  • Blaming the algorithm for ill-conditioning – no method can cure it.
  • Choosing $h$ “as small as possible”.
  • Confusing conditioning with stability.
